summary:
SkyShift is an interactive, web-based cosmic exploration platform developed for the "Planet X and SPHEREx" challenge. NASA’s SPHEREx telescope maps the entire sky four times in 102 infrared wavelengths, unlocking celestial motions otherwise invisible to human eyes. 

SkyShift bridges the gap between complex astrophysical data and public citizen science. The platform transforms real NASA/IPAC IRSA infrared sky cutouts into interactive tools: a dual-epoch Sky Explorer, a historical Blink Comparator (the technique that discovered Pluto) for detecting moving objects like Comet 3I/ATLAS and asteroids, a 102-band infrared wavelength slider, an interactive "Hunt for Planet X" discovery game, and an integrated real-time Gemini-powered conversational space guide.

SkyShift democratizes all-sky infrared astrophysics, empowering students, educators, and citizen scientists to understand how shifting celestial objects reveal hidden bodies across our solar system and beyond.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

SkyShift is an immersive digital observatory and educational platform that brings NASA’s SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer) mission directly to web browsers. SPHEREx photographs the entire celestial sphere across 102 distinct infrared bands every 6 months. SkyShift utilizes actual and modeled multi-epoch infrared data from NASA/IPAC IRSA to let users inspect how celestial bodies shift position over time against stationary background stars:

  • Interactive Sky Explorer: A high-performance canvas engine allowing 0.5x–4x zoom, pan, and real-time epoch toggling across sky fields (including Comet 3I/ATLAS, Orion Nebula, and the Galactic Center).
  • Astronomical Blink Comparator: Recreates the classic discovery technique used by Clyde Tombaugh to discover Pluto, rapidly toggling between temporal observations so moving targets visually flick or jump.
  • 102-Band Wavelength Slider: Dynamically adjusts false-color RGB channels representing SPHEREx's 0.75 µm to 4.5 µm spectral sensitivity, visualizing how dust, stars, and cool planetary candidates react at different infrared spectra.
  • "Hunt for Planet X" Challenge: A gamified discovery module challenging users to locate faint shifting trans-Neptunian candidates under timed observation.
  • SkyShift AI Guide: A conversational agent powered by Google Gemini API providing contextual explanations on infrared astronomy and mission instrumentation.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Demystifies Infrared Astronomy: Translates invisible infrared spectra and high-dimensional spectral data into intuitive false-color visualizations.
  • Zero-Barrier Citizen Science: Runs purely client-side without requiring specialized software (like DS9 or Python astronomy libraries), accessible on mobile, tablet, or desktop.
  • Interactive Pedagogy: Combines gamification with authentic scientific methods (blink comparison), fostering active discovery rather than passive reading.

3. What is the intended impact?

SkyShift aims to expand global engagement with NASA's SPHEREx mission, inspiring students, educators, and amateur stargazers to participate in citizen astronomy. By experiencing how real celestial surveys detect moving asteroids, brown dwarfs, and hypothetical outer-system objects (Planet X), users gain genuine scientific literacy regarding how modern space telescopes uncover the hidden dynamics of our universe.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

  • Frontend: React 19, Vite, GSAP (GreenSock Animation Platform) + ScrollTrigger for motion design.
  • Graphics & Sound: HTML5 Canvas 2D API for data rendering; Web Audio API for custom ambient space drone synthesis.
  • Artificial Intelligence: Google Gemini API via Vercel Edge Serverless functions (/api/chat) with fallback streaming.
  • Astronomical Data Processing: Python 3, Astropy, Astroquery (NASA/IPAC IRSA TAP query interface), Pillow, NumPy.
  • Deployment & Hosting: Vercel Edge Network.

5. How is our project creative?

Rather than presenting static tables or scientific whitepapers, SkyShift presents NASA astrophysics through a modern, curated exhibition aesthetic. It bridges fine arts and hard science using an evocative chromatic palette (Warm Cream, Deep Plum, Acid Lime, Molten Orange), cinematic responsive preloading, an authentic audio synthesizer replicating deep-space frequencies, and interactive tools that emulate genuine observatory hardware.

6. What factors did our team consider?

  • Scientific Accuracy vs. Accessibility: Balancing rigorous multi-epoch coordinates (RA/Dec) and spectral ranges with intuitive controls suitable for non-scientists.
  • Web Performance: Implementing canvas-based rendering and optimized vector math to ensure smooth 60 FPS interactions across lower-spec devices.
  • Ethical AI Integration: Explicitly sandboxing the AI guide with authoritative mission prompts and full transparency disclosures.
